idea: Antipodal 81-pair symmetry search with absolute-value LogSumExp annealing then symmetry-breaking polish
direction: Run a genuinely symmetry-constrained search using 81 antipodal pairs: parameterise only representatives \(y_1,\ldots,y_{81}\in S^7\), construct \(X=(y_1,-y_1,\ldots,y_{81},-y_{81})\), and optimise the maximum over both \(\langle y_i,y_j\rangle\) and \(-\langle y_i,y_j\rangle\) for \(i<j\) (self-antipodal pairs have cosine \(-1\) and are irrelevant), initialising the representatives by greedily pairing points in `best.npy` with nearly antipodal partners and also from random starts; use staged LogSumExp L-BFGS while exactly preserving antipodality, then unfold the best symmetric candidate and spend the final 25–35 seconds on unconstrained LP polishing so symmetry can break if beneficial, thereby enforcing balanced mirrored contacts during exploration while not forcing symmetry in the returned code.

idea: E8-root greedy-deletion starts annealed by staged exponential-repulsion L-BFGS with hole repair and LP polish
direction: Search from an algebraically structured $E_8$ seed rather than from the record: construct all 240 $E_8$ roots, namely the 112 vectors with two coordinates $\pm1$ and six zeros and the 128 vectors with all coordinates $\pm1/2$ and an even number of minus signs, then obtain 162-point starts by greedily deleting 78 roots, at each deletion removing a point with largest row-max and then largest contact count (with several randomised tie-breaking runs), as well as by taking a few random 162-root subsets. This tests whether a much more symmetric and contact-regular configuration, inherited from the 8D kissing configuration rather than from the incumbent basin, can be deformed below $0.495523833137$.

idea: Cavity deletion with joint L-BFGS reinsertion always including the rattler, then smooth refinement and short LP polish.
direction: Implement cavity deletion-and-joint-reinsertion correctly, always including the rattler: identify the zero-contact point, points with at least 20 contacts, and points whose row-max is tied, then repeatedly delete sets of $k\in\{3,4,6,8,10\}$ chosen as (rattler plus highest-contact points), (one spatial/contact-graph cluster), or random mixtures, freeze the remaining $162-k$ points, and place the deleted points initially at distinct holes found from 50,000 random sphere samples followed by local minimisation of their maximum cosine to the frozen code. Jointly optimise only the $8k$ coordinates of the free points with L-BFGS on a log-sum-exp objective over free--frozen and free--free pairs, using temperatures $0.01,0.003,0.001$ and about 150 iterations per temperature, then unfreeze all points for a short smooth refinement and a 3--5 second trust-region LP polish. Run many cavity choices until about 150 seconds, keep every post-LP result, and return the best; this directly attacks overloaded points while allowing several replacements to cooperate rather than greedily reinserting one point at a time.

direction: Crawl along the jammed contact manifold using an explicit tangent-space nullspace calculation: build a $7\times8$ orthonormal tangent basis for each point by SVD, express displacements in the resulting 1134 tangent coordinates, form the Jacobian $A$ whose row for a contact $(i,j)$ is the tangent projection of $x_j-\langle x_i,x_j\rangle x_i$ at $i$ and the corresponding projection of $x_i-\langle x_i,x_j\rangle x_j$ at $j$ for pairs with slack below $10^{-6}$, and compute the smallest singular directions of the dense matrix $A$ with `numpy.linalg.svd`. Repeat from the best crawl point with new random null directions, reserving the final 20 seconds for full LP polishing; unlike a first-order LP step, these moves preserve existing contacts to first order and let second-order effects create and destroy contacts.

idea: Deletion-regrowth continuation from the rattler-first jammed code down to 152 points with LP repolish then greedy largest-hole reinsertion with per-point balanced log-sum-exp smoothing and LP polish across four removal orders.
direction: Use deletion--regrowth continuation in the number of points to force a global redistribution: starting from the incumbent, remove the rattler first and then successively remove lowest-contact or randomly chosen points to produce optimised codes of sizes 161 down to about 152, LP-polishing each smaller code (which should attain a materially lower maximum because it is under-full), then reinsert points one at a time at continuously optimised largest holes, after each insertion running a per-point-balanced smooth phase that minimises $\sum_i \tau\log\sum_{j\ne i}\exp((\langle x_i,x_j\rangle-C)/\tau)$ for $\tau=0.005,0.002,0.0007$ in addition to the global maximum, followed by LP polish. Try rattler-first, lowest-contact, highest-contact, and random removal orders, and return the best completed 162-point code after a final 20-second LP polish; the balanced row objective prevents the reinserted points from remaining slack while a hard core retains the old maximum.

Evolve a diverse population of jammed optima from random, E8-subset and perturbed starts with Riesz plus LogSumExp annealing, then recombine pairs after Procrustes-Hungarian alignment with spatial-half and best-local mixing plus hole-repair and LP polish.
direction: Build a diverse elite population and recombine genuinely different local optima. Generate multiple optima from random, low-discrepancy, $E_8$-subset, and heavily perturbed starts using Riesz-energy annealing over several exponents and LogSumExp refinement, recording their Gram spectra and contact-graph fingerprints so near-duplicates are rejected. For selected parent pairs, align the second parent by orthogonal Procrustes rotation followed by Hungarian point matching, then form children by taking complementary spatial halves, random matched subsets, or individually better-matched points from each parent; greedily replace any point creating a pair well above the target and repair the child with smooth optimization plus LP. Maintain perhaps $8$ diverse elites, iterate recombination for most of the time budget, and return the best child or incumbent, thereby combining partial structures that no single-basin perturbation can reach.

idea: Delete the rattler plus highest-contact overloaded points to create voids, relax the smaller code with staged exponential repulsion and trust-region LP, then greedily reinsert points into refined largest spherical holes with short smooth-plus-LP repair over multiple random orders while keeping the best 162-point code.
direction: Use deletion–reinsertion size continuation that temporarily makes the problem easier. Remove the rattler together with $k\in\{4,8,12,20\}$ highest-contact or most overloaded points, optimize the remaining $162-k$ points with staged exponential repulsion and LP until their maximum cosine is substantially below the target, then reinsert points one at a time at the largest spherical hole found from at least $50{,}000$ random candidates plus local maximization of the minimum angle. After each insertion run short smooth optimization and LP polishing, allowing a temporary increase above the incumbent and using several random insertion orders rather than discarding a branch after its first worsening. This explicitly creates and fills voids, rewires contacts around formerly overloaded points, and should always retain and return the best feasible $162$-point configuration encountered.
